entries.name: Privacy initiative (KPI)
entries.note: Community research by @WellerOlaf on optional privacy for native KAS. Not Kaspa core, not a KIP. main 98aa99fa (4 Oct 11:24:38Z), Apache-2.0, created 2 Oct, 11 commits, one author, code written with AI agents, unaudited. A0.5 on Testnet 10: a 10.2 tKAS P2SH reserve paid out once through a Groth16 BN254 proof checked by OpZkPrecompile (0xa6, Groth16 tag 0x20; KIP-16), plus introspection from KIP-10 (input/output count, amounts, output script), KIP-17 (outpoint txid/index, OpCat/OpSubstr/OpNum2Bin) and KIP-20 (OpOutputAuthorizingInput 0xd6, only to require an unbound payout). No KIP-20 covenant id (covenant=None). Release tx 29d875bb…b554 in chain block c38a5439 (3 Oct 17:56:48Z), accepted by c8dc02dd; spends 67aab5bf…:0 (1,020,000,000 sompi); fee 0.2 tKAS; BLAKE2b-256 of the 576-byte redeem equals the P2SH hash; checked on the desk's synced TN10 node 4 Oct 18:01 and 18:18 CEST. Desk build (log-based): 7/7 Rust, 28 invalid variants rejected, 13/13 Node on Node 22; draft PR #22 (A1) 20/20 Rust at 2590e392, G5 open, G6 not run. 5 Oct: #22 head f4a4ddc5 records the author's failed TN10 live attempt 1 of 4 Oct (S0 funded and S0 -> S1 accepted, boundary receipt failed, independent recovery not run, S1 exited by a separate terminal tx); author's record, txids not desk-checked. Single-party trusted setup per claim. Not a privacy pool: no notes, nullifiers, private transfers or anonymity yet. His 4 Oct architecture post is design only. X backfill 6 Sep to 4 Oct: 6 to 30 Sep searched by keyword only. 8 Oct: the author's A1 official trial record (draft #22, head fb8a5017) reports PASS for the scoped autonomous S1 recovery on TN10: A switched off, B started after independent C saw A gone, rediscovered S1, made a fresh Groth16 proof, paid out 8.1 test KAS (terminal 085f8fa5…0ff83). Not the full G5/G6 gates; txids not desk-checked. main 5435113d after #25 (post-quantum research) and #26 (agents testnet practice). 9 Oct: #22 (A1) merged 8 Oct 18:22:45Z as e4a10390; main ccbdfbc7 (8 Oct 19:52Z) after docs/research #27 to #29. entries.name: kaspa-x402 (elldeeone)
entries.note: Bind the RC2 tag, not `main`. On the tag, `docs/versioning-policy.md` names four-byte KCC-01 dispatch tags once, beside SilverScript `3ed9733`. The portable artifact reports compiler version `0.1.0`. That stamp is the known v1.0.0 compiler stamp. It does not flip KCC-1 to Final. Fixture entry tags are this covenant's own: escrow claim `23959b42`, topUp `ae09679c`, refund `17a2027b`; hash-chain borrow `c6e1d705`, ownerRotate `60104a23`, ownerSweep `89d59c06`. They are not the KCC-1 example vectors `2c49ed65` and `676b1a86`, and they are not KCC-20. The tag's template-id list omits `kaspa-x402-hash-chain-head-v1`. The same file's version paragraph and the contract include that id. `cb769b17` https://github.com/elldeeone/kaspa-x402/commit/cb769b171e6ee4f9c74577c014c3d00aa855053c adds it to the list. `kaspa:mainnet` in that doc is a reserved profile name. The validation target is `kaspa:testnet-10`. npm `latest` stays on the earlier alpha. The four public packages are `1.0.0-rc.2` on the `rc` tag. What open #22 (head 06532aada4506b60668b84127047b88bc9ad4fb6; new templates and the rest are in the x402 bind the tag row) would leave stale in the public STP-KAS x402 write-ups. Desk git grep on 2 Oct: x402-vs-grok 405e643f, grok-heavy-test e2a02e21 and three-x-reviews 985de50f name template kaspa-x402-escrow-v4. x402-ishum 8a1dc4c0 only says escrow-v4 (short form) in its comparison table. x402-vs-grok and grok-heavy-test also pin the v4 source SHA-256 065dff5d (the PR's escrow-v5 source is 9f25f3f7) and say a top-up needs SIGHASH_ALL from both parties. grok-heavy-test patches/windows-clone-and-test.patch targets the v4 paths and constants and would not apply on #22. Fork STP-KAS/kaspa-x402 168973e5 (22 Sep) carries the SIGHASH_ALL byte check in contracts/kaspa-x402-escrow-v4.sil L50, L104, L106, L139. These write-ups describe rc.1 and stay true for the RC2 tag; if #22 merges they describe the earlier templates. No STP-KAS repo hard-codes kaspa-x402-hash-chain-head-v1. Nothing changed in those repos. Bind prerelease v1.0.0-rc.2 (tag 724c5fff22de500fcf729c43b59d25036fbffa9c, published 2026-10-01T03:40:35Z). GitHub latest-release returns 404 because it is a prerelease. Annotated tag object 35f011d peels to that commit. Bind the peel. The author's rc2-evidence.json records an earlier same-number source b73caadf (annotated object 353db437, commit time 2026-10-01T00:15:01Z). The diff to the peel is hosted PNN evidence under packages/demo-gateway, the worker check script, and docs. It does not touch the public client, core, covenant, or server trees. That file says the public npm tarballs are byte-identical. This desk did not re-hash npm. main is 3 commits ahead at cb769b171e6ee4f9c74577c014c3d00aa855053c (2026-10-01T04:25:57Z). Those commits change site scripts, site CSS, package.json, specs, and docs. They do not change packages/ or contracts/. The site is built from that commit. The release source is the peel. The tag hash-chain spec still says the profile is not a published release profile, and that the draft does not put paymentFlow upfront on existing exact offers. Tag direct-server.ts already sets upfront, and the exact HTTP vectors include it. The site spec matches the code. It is not the tag text. Still not v1.0.0. Still not mainnet. Native KAS. The public scheme enum is exact and batch-settlement. Exact stays kaspa-exact-v2. Batch stays kaspa-escrow-v3, template kaspa-x402-escrow-v4. Hash-chain is an optional exact binding, kaspa-hash-chain-exact-v1, template kaspa-x402-hash-chain-head-v1, a one-use grant on a KIP-20 head. Not a third scheme. Not a KCC-20 token. The browser demo vendors kaspa-wasm 2.0.0. The optional Node host loads sdkModule from private config. The documented example points that path at a 2.0.0 build. Consensus vectors record rusty-kaspa 2.1.0 at 01b532e8. The envelope name kaspa-sdk-safe-json-v2.0.0 is the JSON name. In scripts/hash-chain-demo.mjs the UTXO read uses the configured node. The selected-chain view defaults to https://api-tn10.kaspa.org and posts /transactions/search for acceptance. That public index is not the hosted PNN path. Voucher digest is sha256 of sha256(utf8 kaspa:x402:escrow-voucher:v3), sha256 of the network string, the raw covenant id, and the cumulative as le64. The fixture domainTagHash is cb645ce99ebb74afb1f1e3a73e0462249ee42cd9edfcd55723e7291af0292570 and this desk recomputed that sha256. A zero covenant id is rejected. Batch claim pays the merchant at most the claim and takes the fee inside it. The claim stays below the lane. The hash-chain covenant borrow requires only a larger output 0. It does not check the quoted price. hash-chain-verifier.ts requires the successor amount to equal the previous head plus the quote. An underpaid spend can still be consensus-valid and move the head without becoming an accepted payment. An abandoned underpay in the grant tests ends at needsRotation. ownerSweep takes the fee from the pile and the head id dies. On the tag, docs/versioning-policy.md names four-byte KCC-01 dispatch tags once, beside SilverScript 3ed9733. The portable artifact reports compiler version 0.1.0. That does not make KCC-1 Final. Fixture entry tags are this covenant's own: escrow claim 23959b42, topUp ae09679c, refund 17a2027b; hash-chain borrow c6e1d705, ownerRotate 60104a23, ownerSweep 89d59c06. They are not the KCC-1 example vectors 2c49ed65 and 676b1a86, and they are not KCC-20. The tag template-id list omits kaspa-x402-hash-chain-head-v1. The same file's version paragraph and the contract include that id. main adds it to the list. kaspa:mainnet there is a reserved profile name. npm latest stays on the earlier alpha. The four public packages are 1.0.0-rc.2 on the rc tag. Hosted https://demo.kaspa-x402.org/health on this 1 Oct 2026 read reported releaseVersion 1.0.0-rc.2 and chainEvidenceSource pnn. Canary checkedAt 2026-10-01T07:15:40.524Z was ok (virtual DAA 585075695, wss://vector-10.kaspa.green). Paid canaries skipped. /hash-chain/status was ready, head version 1, 220000000 sompi. Author rc2-evidence.json (sourceCommit 724c5fff): the 18 funded flows are exact and batch, completed 2026-10-01T03:29:38.675Z. None of those 18 is named hash-chain. Hosting records three browser hash-chain payments, including a retry after redeploy. Native replay in that file is HTTP 200. A cross-resource replay is HTTP 409. CI run 36810525945 succeeded on 724c5fff. Offline consensus check recorded 2026-09-30 against rusty-kaspa 2.1.0 at 01b532e8b553. One configured public-node set. Not independent corroboration. Not quorum. An abandoned grant can still need operator head rotation. Catalog: https://x.com/KaspaScopio/status/2105516728402727289. 2 Oct: open https://github.com/elldeeone/kaspa-x402/pull/22 head 06532aad — allow signer-chosen sighash types in the covenants (drop SIGHASH_ALL-only; reference signing still defaults to SIGHASH_ALL). It adds new templates, escrow-v5 and hash-chain-head-v2: template IDs and compiled scripts change, and existing heads and channels cannot upgrade in place (sweep or settle/refund them, then create new state). The PR body says the funded Testnet-10 proof against the final reviewed commit is still pending; published RC2 evidence covers the earlier templates. Not merged. Not on the RC2 tag. 8 Oct: #22 merged to main 7 Oct 05:47:20Z as 3f7b6df2 (head 7ada3009), not on a tag; latest tag still the prerelease v1.0.0-rc.2 (releases/latest 404). #23 to #27 merged 7 Oct: exact profiles require paymentFlow "upfront" plus a simulated request-binding prototype (#23), protocol workspace split (#24, #25), funded-proof tooling with a 40,000,000-sompi fee guard and an escrow-v5/head-v2 evidence index on one Testnet-10 node (#26; no independent-node or mainnet claim), docs (#27). main d81f58a3. Kas-Smiths post 405 (Seb287, 8 Oct): variable pricing request from his own mainnet pay-per-request site; his numbers, claim. 9 Oct: #28 (harden payment authorization and exact retries) merged 9 Oct 00:12:42Z as 36f5136c, now main; author's PR text. Latest tag still the prerelease v1.0.0-rc.2 (releases/latest 404).

entries.name: Satoshi's Engine (essay)
entries.note: kaspaexplained.com/satoshis-engine.pdf https://kaspaexplained.com/satoshis-engine.pdf, by Moose.kas (@THEMOOSEISLOOS5). 89 pages. The PDF metadata says it was created 21 Sep 2026; no version is stated. sha256 `4062170b0d53aece…`. Read 26 Sep 2026. An essay on proof-of-work mining economics: the boom-and-bust cycle between coin price and mining cost, cost of production as a floor under price, and two one-way trends (more work behind each coin, less energy per unit of work). It names no network (p. 6) and makes no Kaspa protocol claim, so nothing in it conflicts with this board. Its main claim, that a coin costs more to produce each cycle, is reasoned rather than measured, and the author lists the fee handover and the demand floor as open questions (pp. 86–88). Desk notes: `SATOSHIS-ENGINE.md` https://github.com/STP-KAS/kaspa-master-file/blob/cf10a0f53dc98279f12cd523be008879efff00fd/SATOSHIS-ENGINE.md. Catalog, not a pin.

entries.name: KASRANKS
entries.note: GitHub user KASRANKS, created 23 Mar 2026, four public repos. Browser apps on kaspa.Resolver plus api.kaspa.org. KASSWORD 8af2e17 (28 Aug): six-branch P2SH locker, selectors 0x01 Schnorr, 0x02 HLMT, 0x03 HTLC, 0x04 DMS, 0x06 PQ-cold, 0x05 recovery. Keyless branches pin one input, one output, BLAKE2b of OpTxOutputSpk (version u16 big-endian plus script), and output amount >= input minus 0.05 KAS. entries.name: 1984 (stp's Testnet-10 village square)
entries.note: sixpack.wtf/1984.html is a Testnet-10 village square. Page code STP-KAS/sixpack.wtf 571bffcfbafe2467c667b6c12ecfee4eb4f3b8aa. Liftoff, What do you think about AI, and Joint address are on Random and on the cinema reel. The films before launch are twice the earlier size. One stands left of the rocket and one stands right. The balances stay in the top right, on the square, in a shop, in the cinema, and on a flight. Bank is on that card. Open the tx opens that Testnet 10 transaction. In orbit the sky is dark and the stars show. The Moon, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn are photographs. The Moon map is NASA. Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and the rings are Solar System Scope, CC BY 4.0. Original Ashfields. tKAS is the coin that moves. POCencept and KUSDT are ledger tags. A KUSDT freeze leaves the other two spendable. The landing gate is Kasware, Kastle, and a one-time funded test address. The same wallet opens its history. A shop uses one rail and one Buy button. Lock asks Kasware or Kastle when that wallet is the address on the page. The wallet signs only a tKAS swap. A shop buy, and a POCencept or KUSDT swap, ask on the page, then OK. The wallet reads the six-times fee from the till. Walking into a building fades the view. A gold ring marks the next step. The card waits. A paid shop redraws the balances on that card. A shop purchase shows Paid. Buying the roadster shows Parked. Getting in shows You drive. A lap shows One lap. Lux's cinema is the dark building west of the lot. Take a seat, then the screen. One ticket of 5.00 toy dollars plays the reel. Prev, Next, and Shuffle move the reel. Overview lists every film. Each film keeps its own width and height inside the glass. Every counter, the cinema ticket, the snacks, and a hop offer tKAS, POCencept, and KUSDT. What are the rails? opens the short note. That button is the opener on the whole square. Snacks are toy tags while it runs. The thin bar lists all three. The bank card opens when you click a clerk. Push tKAS, POCencept, or KUSDT. Each bank window says its name once. The open clerk swaps into the other two. The books desk explains locked coins and the practice purse. While a tKAS swap is opening, the steps stay on that clerk. The owned roadster waits on the lot in front of Pike's shop. Drive in your roadster is the large gold button. Once you are in the car, Launch into space is the gold button. Get out is the gold button. Thrusters show while it moves. Launch, while you are in the car and outside, waits for the two tower films, then the countdown. The ship leaves the pad when that count reaches zero, and the longer comms play then. The car then leaves the ship. A bar fills until the car is out. End the flight shows then. Simulation theory shows only after that click. The button warns that it brings you back to the simulation on Earth. The countdown starts when the second film ends. The ship lifts when that count reaches zero, and End the flight stops the comms. The history in the left corner is taller and it scrolls. Back on the square, the same sentence is in that corner and in large type: You are back on the square, in the roadster. You returned to a simulation of a simulation of a simulation, 255524 deep. KONI stays off the ship for the whole flight. The way to the Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, or the abyss is ten seconds. Those worlds fill the window the way the Earth does. Once you arrive, the same rails can send you to another world, or into the abyss. The flight card sits in the bottom corner. Reaching orbit and the ejection keep that Earth in the window. The ship coasts for ten seconds before the roadster leaves. Out there the two cars race in orbit around the Earth, and the talk is how beautiful and wonderful the Gulf of America is. The Moon, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn fill the window the way the Earth does. The car stays above Saturn's rings. Through T+ 0:15 the booster stays on the ship. The line on the hull says the booster is on the ship, then the booster lets go along the stack. The ship pulls ahead, the booster peels off and flips, and it lights a boostback burn. The left tower film plays, then the right one. A bar fills across both lengths and says time before launch. The countdown starts when the second film ends. When the booster lets go, that separation plays its voice while the ship and the booster stay on screen. The stack stands on the launch mount. One tower stands beside it, and the chopsticks stay open. The comms stop when the roadster leaves the bay. The hop card sits in the right corner, tall enough to show the hops, and the joke line stays on that card. A shop slip stays open so you can open the tx or buy again. After a hop, the slip says Close this tab and stays on the flight. The roadster can be bought again. Log out returns to the welcome gate and keeps the wallet saved on this browser. Exit to the square is on the shop, the bank, Hunt Hall, and the cinema. Close puts the card away. POCencept and KUSDT are named stables. The economics page says this page is an experiment. Nothing here is really useful. Economics sits in the tab row immediately before 1984. The landing page and the welcome gate say 1984 is early development. A new clip is in the cinema and on Random. Liftoff burns a column from the bells. Launch is the large gold button. The opening lines stay Countdown, Liftoff, and Climbing out. The prices stay toy dollars. Pike sells the roadster for 1.00 toy dollar. Click the ground to point where you walk, or use the keyboard. Buy the roadster and it parks on the lot. W A S D move the way you look. The arrow keys do too. Esc closes the card, then leaves the room. Every 1984 send pays six times the ordinary Testnet 10 fee. The quiet standard is 100 sompi per gram, so a quiet quote pays 600. The flat wallet fee is 0.06 tKAS. Guest funding, a guest payment, a sweep, and a redeem use that rate. The faucet payout stays 0.6 tKAS. The faucet miner fee stays twice the ordinary rate. You walk into the building. In the cafe, and at the table, you take a seat and the menu blinks, or you order at the counter. The market opens at the counter. Pike or the sign opens the roadster shop. A lock the public list does not show is read from a synced node, about the last minute of accepted blocks. That public list records accepted txs again (1 Oct 2026 16:24 UTC, cache-busted /info/health: database synced, accepted-tx clock 3 s behind). It is still not proof a payment landed. Use a funded test address opens 50000 tKAS from Grok's Testnet-10 wallet. The welcome card does not show that amount. If that is not instant, the gate lists each step while the small coins are joined. One thousand can be opened in a day. On a phone, drag a finger to look, tap the ground to walk, and Step moves you. A phone wallet cannot switch to Testnet 10 from the page. The live quote and the reserve address sit on the bank's fine line. KCC-20 stays Draft. There is no spendable L1 stable. The shop card says this buy is this square's own ledger. There is no covenant transaction. It is not Argent or SilverScript, and it is not a vProg tic-tac-toe ply. A tKAS bank swap says the txid is the Testnet 10 payment. Why, what, and how: STP-KAS/1984-why-what-how 67984ca3be67887008daae770fab395c78a6a2f9. 1984 4312844c425bad4b3e06d50013d2248cabedb0ec, 1984-rails 8a268de6daa630fa85b22a8a008cf164ff690b5f, and 1984-prompts 52fd8bb8a786aebc864967be4da0c1fc739b9cae point there. The spend plan for Grok Ask and Grok Bot is ask-and-bot 3abd929fabc2bf51b70b10cc551e268bcd42dab2. Reed's Hunt Hall is the timber building east of the lot. Click Reed, then the board. Promise is not Buy. The pack stays hidden until a subset pays. The banner is Pack paid on this square. The guide states the ceiling. The goal of a peer-to-peer chain is a settlement between two people, including while almost nobody takes the coin. The ceiling is a till a stranger can receive on. That bill is a car, an AI service, a game purchase, or a rented service. The cinema card sits on the left of the film. The current film stays up until the next one has a picture. Proof of stake hands the next block to coins already held. Kaspa is proof of work. It sequences the coin now. Sequencing applications on that work is in process. This square is the classroom under that ceiling. The longer note is in a private repo and is not linked here. A Staghunt for a real bill waits until a POC-style coin or a tether-style coin, or both, can be received on Kaspa. The village tags are the classroom. Catalog. Not a product.

RossKU/kob notes at 9d8030c9 (8 Oct 13:12:28Z) and his 8 Oct Core R&D Telegram replies (13:14Z to 13:56Z): hand-written KobAsk.sil 1,684 B vs an idiomatic Argent port 2,705 B (+1,021); with his listed rows removed both are 1,584 B; most of the gap is become rebuilding the whole state. Measured against argent b312deda plus his two patches, not master 9a9f4b10. Splice idea KobAsk.splice1.sil 1,713 B (+29), only for fixed-width fields, the same actor and fields not reassigned before become. cancel ... emits none is the only behavioural difference in his 1,004 tests. Importer artifact id pin (his item 12): the interface fingerprint excludes the handle; open argent#69 (head 435fa89a, opened 8 Oct 14:52:06Z, no review). 244 live stack bindings: only the continuation pin on the 2+2 swap goes over; they omit it. Until argent#61 they store the raw template hash and lengths. The master keeps one Argent sentence tied to #69 with a pointer here.

entries.name: Argent: desk results (8 Oct)
entries.note: Third-party, not audited, demo; desk-tested by stp's bots on 8 Oct (rustc 1.98.1). 232c6ee6 vs 9a9f4b10: only the stones example artifact changes; Player sil_template_hash 80 10 96 97 -> 9f 1f 68 01, artifact id 7133efc5... -> e843bab4...; the other nine example apps are byte-identical and the regenerated trees match the committed examples/build. At 03d67021 require(!controller_id.co_spent()) fails to compile with a type mismatch while the parenthesized form compiles; at 9a9f4b10 both compile. Argent itself stays in the master; not a master row.
